# ConfigMap and Secret Reload on Content Change

Kubernetes does not restart Pods when the content of a mounted ConfigMap
or Secret changes. The mounted file on disk updates (eventually, via
kubelet sync), but processes that read the file once at startup keep the
old content in memory until the Pod restarts for some other reason.

This is a recurring class of bug across charts and homegrown manifests.
Pick a reload strategy explicitly per workload — do not assume "GitOps
applied my change, therefore the app sees it."

## Strategies, most sustainable first

### 1. Cluster-wide controller (preferred)

Install [stakater/Reloader](https://github.com/stakater/Reloader) once,
opt workloads in by annotation. Reloader watches ConfigMap/Secret events
and patches the consumer Deployment (or StatefulSet, DaemonSet, etc.) to
trigger a rolling restart.

Opt-in annotation on the consumer workload:

```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true"
```

This watches every CM and Secret the Pod mounts **directly**.

### 2. Per-chart `checksum/configmap` Helm helper

Many community charts embed:

```yaml
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checksum/config: {{ include (print $.Template.BasePath "/configmap.yaml") . | sha256sum }}
```

Any change to the ConfigMap content changes the checksum, which changes
the Pod template hash, which forces a rollout. Works without an extra
controller but only covers ConfigMaps the chart author opted to hash.

### 3. Manual `kubectl rollout restart`

Defeats GitOps automation and requires human intervention every time
config changes. Use only as an emergency manual override, never as the
documented day-2 procedure.

## Sub-gotcha: indirect ConfigMap references

Reloader's `auto: "true"` only watches CMs and Secrets that the Pod
mounts **directly** (via `volumes:` referencing the resource by name).

ConfigMaps that reach a Pod **indirectly** are invisible to auto-detect.
Example: grafana's `sc-datasources` sidecar watches the cluster for
ConfigMaps with a label, reads them, and writes the merged result into a
shared `emptyDir` volume. The grafana container only mounts the
emptyDir — it never mounts the source ConfigMap. Reloader sees no link.

For indirect references, name the ConfigMap explicitly:

```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    configmap.reloader.stakater.com/reload: "<cm-name>,<other-cm-name>"
```

The same pattern works for Secrets via
`secret.reloader.stakater.com/reload`.

## When to apply

- Any new workload that consumes a ConfigMap or Secret whose content
  changes during the cluster's lifetime (datasources, scrape configs,
  feature flags, TLS material, sealed-secret-derived credentials).
- Any chart bump where the chart introduces a new ConfigMap the workload
  reads at startup.

## When skipping is acceptable

- ConfigMaps that are only read by init containers (the init runs every
  Pod start, so the next restart picks up the change naturally — though
  the restart still needs a trigger).
- Workloads designed to watch their config file at runtime and reload
  in-process (rare; verify in the upstream docs before assuming).
